convention_avoided: gear-shop compatibility table with green ticks and red crosses, or a chat bubble answering in prose
metaphor: the focusing screen seen through an SLR viewfinder: ground glass with a split-image prism in the centre. The image stays sheared until focus is right, then the halves line up.
design_code: Quotes enter sheared and align only when the server finds them verbatim in a manufacturer record, because a split-image prism shows focus by alignment, and this product shows truth by alignment with the source.
An unverified quote stays split with chromatic fringing, because a misaligned prism edge is exactly where real glass throws colour; colour appears only where something is wrong.
The reading surface is lit ground glass inside a black viewfinder surround, because that is where a photographer judges focus.
The verdict is marked with AF-point squares per shooting mode, because viewfinder, live view and video focus with different systems on the same body.
anti_brief: green check / red cross compatibility grid
a camera-shop product card with a lens photo
expressive_axis: motion: the split-image resolve on every quote
structure: viewfinder: black surround, one ground-glass screen, AF-point row per shooting mode, finder LCD strip along the bottom carrying the measured number

edge_depth.depth: glass: inner vignette + grain + faint fresnel rings; surround flat
